Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

phaseR (development version)

  • The Cholesky factor of correlated random effects with three or more coefficients is named in the order the likelihood and VarCorr() read it (by column: L_..._1_1, L_..._2_1, L_..._3_1, L_..._2_2, …). The names followed the rows, so L_..._2_2 labelled the draws of L_31.

  • waic() and loo() compute the pointwise log likelihood with the forward recursion the backends fit with. The R copy of the recursion they used knew only two Gaussian phases without random effects, so for models with random effects, Poisson or binomial outcomes or more than two phases it evaluated a different model (random effects at zero, every outcome Gaussian, two phases).

  • The Laplace backend integrates random effects out before it looks for a mode. It approximated the joint posterior of all parameters by a Gaussian at its mode, but with random effects that mode does not exist: the SDs are already parameterised by their logarithm with the Jacobian included, yet as a random-effect SD shrinks with its effects at zero, the Normal density of the G effects grows like SD^-G while a proper SD prior times the Jacobian falls only like SD. The optimiser ran towards zero SD and the Hessian there was singular (“Hessian not invertible, using pseudo-inverse”, a ridge and an eigenvalue shift then made it invertible). The marginal posterior of the other parameters, with the effects integrated out by the Laplace formula (Tierney and Kadane 1986, as in INLA and TMB: the mode of the effects given the parameters, and the log determinant of the negative Hessian in the effects there), is bounded and has a proper mode. The backend maximises it with its exact gradient (third derivatives by forward-mode dual numbers through the exact gradient of the log posterior), takes the covariance from the Hessian of the log marginal, and draws the effects given the parameters from their Gaussian, linearised in the parameters. The ridge, the pseudo-inverse and the eigenvalue shift are gone; a Hessian that is not positive definite now stops the fit with a message. On a random-intercept model (60 units x 5 times, 10 sites) Laplace means agree with NUTS within 0.5 posterior SD (0.75 for the skewed log SDs of the random effects) and its SDs within a factor of 1.25 (1.5). Models without random effects get the same Gaussian at the joint mode as before.

  • The Laplace backend searches the posterior mode from data-informed starting points instead of all-zero parameters, and NUTS chains start from them. A phase model’s posterior has a mode in which no unit enters a phase and that phase’s parameters sit at their prior; from zeros, far from the data, the optimiser stopped there (60 units x 4 times from sim_phaseR(seed = 8): active intercept -0.003 with SD 2.5 under Laplace, 8.15 with SD 0.23 under NUTS), and so could a NUTS chain. Each starting point fits every phase’s regression (Gaussian, Poisson or logistic, ridge-stabilised) and every transition’s logistic regression to a provisional phase assignment: one splits each unit into equal runs, the others draw each unit’s moves at random from seed. Laplace optimises from n_starts of them (default 5) and keeps the highest log posterior, reported in diagnostics$start_values; NUTS chain c starts at the c-th. Both are reproducible from seed, and R’s random number stream outside the fit is left untouched.

  • Both backends use the exact gradient of the log posterior instead of finite differences. The backward recursion over the latent phases gives the derivative of each unit’s log likelihood with respect to its emission and transition terms (the posterior probabilities of each phase and each move), and the chain rule carries it through the outcome families, the linear predictors, the random-effect parameterisations and the priors. Tests compare it with Richardson-extrapolated central differences on sixteen models (relative error below 1e-6). On the README example (100 units x 5 times, 2 chains x 1000 iterations) NUTS takes 6.5 s instead of 67.5 s at the same minimum ESS (721 against 734), and the Laplace optimiser gets the gradient through optim(gr = ).

  • Random-effect terms whose grouping factor varies within a unit, such as (1 | year) crossed with units, now add the effect of each observation’s own level. The likelihood used the level of the unit’s first observation at every time, so a crossed year effect acted as an effect of the first year. Random slopes without an intercept, (0 + x | group), now multiply their covariate; the likelihood added them as random intercepts.

  • All model families evaluate their likelihood through one forward recursion over the latent phases (src/phase_process.h) and one model description (src/phase_model.h): K ordered phases, one logistic transition predictor per consecutive pair, one dynamics predictor per phase with a Gaussian, Poisson or binomial outcome, and random-effect terms on any predictor. The five likelihood files that each carried their own copy of the recursion are gone; log posteriors of every model kind agree with the previous code to 1e-10 at fixed parameters (tests/testthat/fixtures).

  • Uncorrelated random slopes, (1 + x || group), now give the effects of coefficient j the prior Normal(0, sigma_j). The prior read the SD of each effect from a position that moved with the effect, past the SD block and past the end of the parameter vector.

  • prior now applies to every model family under both backends. The HMC backend, and the Laplace backend for GLM, k-phase, crossed random-effect and random-slope models, evaluated hard-coded priors and ignored prior. Both backends now evaluate one log posterior per model (posterior_target()), whose prior comes from prior(). The hard-coded priors differed from the documented defaults, so default fits of those models change: residual SDs get Half-Normal(0, 1) on the SD instead of Normal(0, 1) on its logarithm, random-effect SDs Half-Normal(0, 0.5) instead of Normal(0, 0.5) on the logarithm, and correlated random slopes LKJ(2) instead of LKJ(1). Under Poisson and binomial families the unused residual SDs now get the sigma prior, which makes their posterior proper.

  • Each phase of a two-phase model now uses the design matrix of its own dynamics() formula in the likelihood. The C++ likelihoods computed the second phase’s mean from the first phase’s design matrix, so fits whose two dynamics() formulas differed estimated the wrong model, and read past the end of the matrix when the second formula had more columns. Predictions, counterfactuals and WAIC already used the per-phase matrices.

  • The HMC backend is the No-U-Turn sampler (Hoffman and Gelman 2014) in Stan’s multinomial form, replacing fixed-length leapfrog trajectories: trajectories double until a U-turn, a divergence or max_treedepth, and warmup adapts the step size by dual averaging and a diagonal metric from the posterior variance in expanding windows. adapt_delta and max_treedepth are passed through ... of fit_phaseR(). One sampler now serves every model family. Fits report divergences after warmup, transitions at maximum tree depth, E-BFMI and the adapted metric.

  • summary() computes the effective sample size with Stan’s multi-chain initial monotone sequence estimator.

  • fit_phaseR() honours seed with the HMC backend: each chain samples from a stream seeded by (seed, chain) that also draws its initial values, so two fits with the same seed return identical draws. With seed = NULL the seed is drawn from R’s random number generator, so set.seed() makes fits reproducible, and the seed used is stored in the fit as fit$seed.

phaseR 0.8.0

Experimental release with feature parity to ratiod.

Features

  • Phase-structured models for longitudinal data
    • k-phase support (arbitrary number of sequential phases)
    • GLM families: Gaussian, Poisson, Binomial
    • Counterfactual inference: ate(), ite(), counterfactual()
  • Random effects
    • Random intercepts: (1 | group)
    • Multiple crossed RE: (1|site) + (1|year)
    • Random slopes: (1 + x | group) and (1 + x || group)
    • Nested RE: (1|site/plot)
  • Inference backends
    • Native HMC/NUTS sampler (no external dependencies)
    • Laplace approximation: backend = "laplace"
  • Custom priors
    • Formula syntax: prior(beta ~ normal(0, 2.5), sigma ~ half_cauchy(1))
    • Distributions: normal(), student_t(), cauchy(), half_normal(), half_cauchy(), lkj()
  • Model comparison
    • WAIC: waic(), compare_waic()
    • LOO-CV via PSIS: loo(), loo_compare()

Core Functions

  • phases(): Declare ordered phases
  • transition(): Specify transition models
  • dynamics(): Specify phase-specific outcome models
  • phase_model(): Compose complete model
  • fit_phaseR(): Fit model
  • posterior_predict(): Posterior predictive simulation
  • fixef(), ranef(), VarCorr(): Extract estimates
  • residuals(), confint(): Diagnostics
